text:
Eli: Quick review: new proposal for series key affordance on multi-line charts. Goal: reduce horizontal clutter while keeping series mapping obvious and accessible. Figma frames: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/series-key-proposals

Priya: Accessibility first: hiding labels entirely is risky. If we show only swatches, we must provide an accessible name per swatch and a clear control to open the full key. Suggest: compact inline key (swatch + 2-3 char abbrev) + a single toggle button that expands to full list. The toggle should be a real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls.

Harper: Visual idea: use an inline compact key above the chart: swatch + short abbrev (like "Auth", "DB") separated by small bullets; follow with a subtle "Show full key" chevron button. On click, an inline drawer reveals full names and a little search. On tiny panels, the drawer becomes a full-width panel under the chart.

Sam: Product note: non-technical viewers prefer full unit names on axes. For units, show parenthetical short label under the axis (e.g., "Users (users/min)") and keep tick values compact. Also prefer outliers to be visible but de-emphasized rather than clipped silently.

Mina: Outlier pattern: show faint off-chart markers for clipped points and a "+n" affordance in the corner. Clicking expands the y-scale. Accessibility: the "+n" should be keyboard focusable and announce how many points are excluded. Example aria-label: "Three points outside visible range. Press Enter to include in scale." Keep the badge visible only when n>0.

Priya: Microcopy + aria suggestions:
- Compact toggle button: aria-label="Toggle series key, 6 series"; when closed announce "Series key collapsed"; when opened announce "Series key expanded, use arrow keys to navigate".
- Swatch items: role="option" with aria-selected state reflecting visibility.
- Outlier badge: aria-live polite updates: coalesce rapid changes, e.g., "2 points included" rather than firing on each toggle.

Harper: Minor UX tweaks:
- Add hover tooltips for abbrevs showing full name.
- Increase hit target for swatches to 40px.
- Add caret on the toggle button so users know it's expandable.
- Keep smoothing control out of the compact key; place in overflow menu; tooltip: "Smooth lines to emphasize trend; may hide spikes." Default off for perf charts.

Eli: Implementation notes for eng:
- Reuse Popover or Drawer components; prefer inline drawer when popover would overflow.
- Implement formatNumberAccessible for aria-labels of tick values (visual "1.2K" -> aria "1,200 requests per minute").
- Add debounce 250ms for aria-live updates.

Sam: Decision proposal summary:
1) Compact inline key (swatch + 2-3 char abbrev) above chart on medium+ widths.
2) A single toggle button (aria-expanded) that reveals an inline drawer with full series list + search.
3) Swatches remain interactive: Enter toggles visibility; arrow keys navigate when drawer open.
4) Outliers shown as de-emphasized markers with a focusable "+n" badge to include them in scale; badge hidden when n=0.
5) Smoothing moved to overflow/advanced controls, default off for perf dashboards.

Priya: I'll post a short QA checklist tomorrow (keyboard order, aria-live checks, tooltip focus). Example SR strings I'll propose: "Series key collapsed. Press Enter to open." and "Four points excluded from scale."

Harper: I'll update the figma frames with the inline drawer variant + tiny-panel fallback.

Mina: I'll mock the outlier marker visuals and a11y states for the badge.
